acceptance: With more than one commit and no TITLE, pr-open never creates a PR titled after the branch name; a test covers this
`make pr-arm` (or pr-ready) refuses to arm a PR whose title equals the branch-derived form, with a fix hint
The pr skill and AGENTS docs mention TITLE
context: Found 2026-10-17: core #3096 merged with the squash subject "chore/remove site from core (#3096)" (364a6e9cd). It had two commits, and the title came from the branch name. That subject can't be changed now. Duplicate pr-open-multi-commit-title-20261017, filed by the tuning agent for the same defect, was dropped in favour of this item.
description: `make pr-open` runs `gh pr create --fill` (Makefile:1164 and :1166). With one commit, --fill uses that commit's subject. With more than one, gh uses the branch name, so a branch like chore/remove-site-from-core becomes the title "chore/remove site from core". The squash merge then keeps it as the permanent develop commit subject, which breaks the Conventional Commits style and the writing standard. Add a TITLE= parameter. When there's more than one commit and no TITLE is given, fail with a clear message, or use the first commit's subject, rather than the branch name. Also check the title on reuse before arming.
